assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Glenmark (consolidated, Rs crore; profit attributable to owners, see tools/authoring/GLENMARK.patch.js). Glenmark reports one segment and revenue by region, so the engine runs one revenue-growth path and one EBITDA-margin path; the regional build sits in `businessLines` and GLENMARK.ctx.js checks it sums to model revenue. FORECASTS ARE CORE: they exclude all ISB 2001 out-licensing income. The US$700mn AbbVie upfront is a one-off (US$525mn booked in Q2FY26, the other US$175mn recognised at US$17.5mn a quarter to Mar-2028 with no cash attached, since the cash came in Sep-2025), so FY27-28E revenue leaves out the ~US$70mn a year of deferred income that reported revenue will still carry, while IGI's ~US$70mn a year of R&D (which that income matches) stays in costs. No milestones or royalties are forecast. Reported FY26 (actual) keeps the Rs3,981.5 cr of licensing income, so FY27E revenue growth is negative on paper. Valued on P/E, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Built by region (businessLines; the script checks the sum). FY26 base Rs16,982.5 cr = core Rs13,001 cr + ISB 2001 income Rs3,981.5 cr. FY27E core Rs16,289 cr (+25% on core; -4.1% on reported FY26): India Rs5,399 cr (+45% on a FY26 base cut by ~Rs1,000 cr of GST-driven destocking in Q2FY26; Q1FY27 Rs1,432 cr, +15.5%; management: over Rs4,800 cr in FY27 and 12-15% a year), North America core US$420mn x Rs95 (FY26 US$357mn; Q1 core +19.8% on gFlovent 44 and other launches; 2-3 respiratory approvals and two sole first-to-files in H2), Europe +9% (guided high single digit), emerging markets +18% (Q1 +27.7%; Ryaltris Brazil and Aumolertinib in H2), other revenue Rs50 cr. Adding back the deferred ISB income (US$70mn, ~Rs665 cr) gives Rs16,954 cr on the reported basis, at the bottom of the Rs17,000-18,000 cr guidance. FY28E +12.5%: India +13%, NA US$460mn (Monroe differentiated injectables, full year of H2FY27 launches, first-to-file exclusivities fading), Europe +11% (guided double digit), EM +14%. FY29E +11.5%: India +13%, NA US$490mn, Europe +11%, EM +13%; inside the 13-15% medium-term CAGR the company targets only if the oncology launches work.

businessLines._why: FY26 revenue by region (AR FY26 segment table): India Rs3,723.7 cr, North America Rs7,139.0 cr = core Rs3,157.5 cr + ISB 2001 income Rs3,981.5 cr (Rs3,670.0 cr booked net in Q2FY26 = US$525mn Rs4,500 cr less Rs830 cr of one-time charges netted in revenue, plus Rs311.5 cr of deferred income in H2, note 19), Europe Rs3,100.7 cr, emerging markets Rs2,940.5 cr, other revenue Rs78.6 cr. Total Rs16,982.5 cr = Screener revenue. North America core in US dollars x an assumed rupee rate (FY26 Rs88.33/$; Q1FY27 Rs94.53).

assumptions._marginWhy: Core EBITDA margin (excluding ISB 2001 income, after IGI's R&D): FY26 core EBITDA Rs591 cr (4.5% of core revenue Rs13,001 cr) was crushed by the India destocking and the one-time IGI bonus and deal costs; H2FY26 core 18.0% (Q3 19.0%, Q4 16.8%); Q1FY27 core 16.6% (reported 20.0% = Rs804.8 cr incl. Rs165.5 cr deferred income). Guidance: 21-22% reported for FY27 (incl. the ~Rs665 cr deferred income, worth ~3.5pp), i.e. ~17.5-18.5% core. FY27E 17.8% core = 21.0% on the reported basis (bottom of guidance: Q1 was 20.0%, freight and API costs up, oncology launch spending). FY28E 19.0% core (~21.9% reported: management's ~1pp improvement from operating leverage, US respiratory and injectables, branded mix). FY29E 19.8%: the deferred income stops in Mar-2028, so reported and core converge; without milestones, the reported margin would fall from ~21.9% to ~19.8% that year. IGI's ~US$70mn a year (about half of group R&D of 7-8% of sales) stays in all three years. Street FY27E: MOSL 20.9%, Choice 21.0% (both reported, incl. deferred income). Each 1pp of FY28E margin is ~Rs183 cr of EBITDA (~6% of EPS).
assumptions._capexWhy: CFO (Q4FY26 call): FY26 was a one-off with 'close to Rs800 cr plus' of intangibles (in-licensing upfronts and milestones for oncology/dermatology, US injectable partnerships) on top of Rs1,358 cr of fixed-asset purchases (Screener); FY27 'around Rs900 cr sort of capex number total'. FY28-29E Rs950 / 1,000 cr (~5% of sales), including further in-licensing milestones (Aumolertinib, Trastuzumab Rezetecan, envafolimab). Acquisitions not modelled.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation, amortisation and impairment Rs573.5 cr; Q1FY27 Rs173 cr (Rs692 cr annualised) after FY26's intangibles and the Rs594 cr of new leases. 5.6% of average gross block (Screener Rs12,072 cr at Mar-26 plus capex) gives Rs701 / 753 / 808 cr for FY27-29E, matching the Q1 run-rate in FY27E.

otherTreasury._why: Debt-like items taken out of the opening net cash (AR FY26 notes 14-18): litigation liabilities and provisions Rs963.6 cr (Rs403.9 cr current and Rs281.6 cr non-current financial liabilities, Rs101.5 cr and Rs176.6 cr provisions; payable over ~2 years per management) and the Rs879.2 cr customer advance (US$96mn received Mar-2026 under a 3.3-year supply contract, to be repaid in product). Model opening net cash = Screener cash Rs1,176 cr + investments Rs42 cr - leases Rs594 cr - Rs1,843 cr = -Rs1,219 cr, against the company's net cash of Rs1,176 cr (which excludes leases and these items). The Rs1,314 cr of ISB 2001 income received in advance is non-cash and is NOT treated as debt; it stays in operating liabilities.

assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied by the engine to the model's net cash when positive (it is negative at Mar-26 after the debt-like items, so it adds nothing in FY27E and a little from FY28E). 5%: FY26 interest income Rs41.3 cr on ~Rs1,200-2,700 cr of average cash; Indian treasury rates ~5-6%.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from AR FY26 note 20 and Q1FY27: (a) interest on operating cash (~Rs800-900 cr held, CFO) Rs40 cr (FY26 Rs41.3 cr); (b) working-capital 'interest-rate arbitrage' income Rs140 / 145 / 150 cr, which the CFO says now sits in other income while the matching cost sits in finance cost (Q1FY27 other income Rs66 cr = ~Rs40 cr arbitrage + ~Rs11 cr interest + ~Rs15 cr misc); (c) miscellaneous income Rs60 / 65 / 70 cr (FY26 Rs60.1 cr). Forex gains (Rs359.2 cr in FY26) and the ISB 2001 income are not forecast. FY27E Rs240 cr vs Rs460.6 cr in FY26 (Rs101 cr ex forex) and Rs264 cr Q1-annualised.
assumptions._interestLabel: Finance cost (leases, bank charges, working-capital arbitrage)
assumptions._interestWhy: No borrowings since Mar-26, but Q1FY27 finance cost was Rs54 cr (Rs216 cr annualised): interest on Rs594 cr of leases (~Rs50 cr a year at ~9%), bank commitment charges and the cost side of the working-capital arbitrage whose income is in other income (CFO). FY26 Rs208.7 cr (bank loans Rs120.8 cr, repaid). Rs215 / 205 / 195 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: Q1FY27 ETR 24.9% (tax Rs160 cr on PBT Rs643 cr); FY25 25.2%; IGI's Swiss/US losses get little tax relief, so the group rate stays above India's 25.2%. MOSL 27.5%. 26% flat.
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend Rs5.0 a share (~10% of reported EPS, ~Rs141 cr cash); FY25 Rs2.5. 8% of core EPS (~Rs5 a share).

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash only after the AbbVie upfront; a history of USFDA warning letters (three sites since 2022), US antitrust settlements in three of the last four years, two India destocking episodes and a loss year (FY24). Ke 12.5%, above Lupin (11.9%) and Cipla (11.3%).
dcf._tgWhy: 5.5%: India 10-12% nominal, emerging markets and Europe high single digit, US generics flat to low single digit in dollars.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 21% core: the branded mix (India, EM, European respiratory and dermatology, oncology in-licensing) lifts margins slowly, but IGI's burn continues unless milestones arrive; the company's own 23% (2022 target) was not met.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex 5% of revenue (FY27E 5.5% incl. in-licensing); depreciation 4% of revenue (FY27E 4.3%).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: The Investor Day plan works: 13-15% growth, US respiratory approvals and the two first-to-files land on time, Monroe ramps, Aumolertinib and Trastuzumab Rezetecan scale in India and EM, Ryaltris heads for US$250-300mn, margins reach ~23%.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: US launches slip (Indore stays under the warning letter, respiratory approvals delayed), another India channel disruption, more US litigation charges and freight/API costs keep core margin near 16-17%.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Glenmark: both brokers that disclose a method use P/E (Motilal Oswal 25x 12-month-forward EPS plus a Rs290 NPV for ISB 2001; Deven Choksey 25x Sep-27E EPS in its Jan-2026 note). 22x = Glenmark's 20.2x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 on EPS before exceptional items and before the ISB 2001 licensing income (batch practice A18; the upfront treated as a one-off), leaving out the trough years FY24 (a loss) and FY26 (core EPS Rs7.2, below half of FY25's Rs47.0), times the pharma sector factor of 1.082 (median of the nine-peer set's trailing P/E at the 30-Sep close vs their five-year medians: +8.2%, PLAYBOOK §7c A20; Glenmark is outside the set) = 21.9x, rounded to the nearest half-turn. No growth or returns adjustment and no separate value for IGI/ISB 2001 (only one of the two brokers that disclose a method adds it; shown as a sensitivity). Bull 34.5x and bear 17.5x: the 75th (31.7x) and 25th (16.2x) percentiles of the same series times the same factor.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Own one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 (EV = price x 28.22 cr shares + Screener net debt at the latest March; EBITDA = next full year, FY26 on a core basis excluding the ISB 2001 income, ours for FY27-28E): median 11.9x leaving out the FY26 trough (core EBITDA Rs591 cr), times the EV/EBITDA analogue of the sector factor for the same nine peers (+7.46%) = 12.8x, rounded to 13x; bull/bear from the 75th/25th percentiles (17.9x / 11.0x). The engine adds the model net cash at Sep-28 (after the debt-like items), a year beyond the target date.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at a 12.5% cost of equity, terminal growth 5.5%, core margin fading to 21%, plus the model's net cash (after debt-like items).

cover.headline: A better company on a stricter yardstick: AbbVie's cheque fixed the balance sheet, but core earnings and Glenmark's own valuation history do not support ₹2,335
cover.lead: Glenmark is India's No.13 drug maker, with leading dermatology, respiratory and cardiac brands, branded businesses in Europe and emerging markets, a US generics arm and a biotech (IGI) that licensed its lead antibody to AbbVie for US$700mn upfront in 2025. That cheque cleared the debt and made FY26 profit (₹1,362 cr) possible despite ₹2,266 cr of exceptional charges. Q1FY27 sales grew 23%, but the core EBITDA margin (excluding US$17.5mn a quarter of deferred licensing income that brings no cash) fell to 16.6%. The stock is ₹2,335: 28.9x our Sep-28E core EPS (26.0x on the street's reported basis). The street values Glenmark on **P/E (25x forward EPS; MOSL adds ₹290 for ISB 2001)**. We forecast core EPS of ₹58.3 / 73.1 / 88.5 for FY27-29E (₹75.7 / 90.9 on the reported basis, in line with MOSL's ₹75.3 / 91.6). Applying **22x to Sep-28E core EPS of ₹80.8** (Glenmark's own forward median of 20.2x since 2021 on EPS before exceptional items and licensing income, leaving out the FY24 and FY26 troughs, re-rated by the pharma sector's +8.2%) gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹1,811, DCF ₹1,321. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: Reported earnings flatter Glenmark until March 2028
arguments.p: US$175mn of the AbbVie upfront, already received in cash, is being booked as revenue at US$17.5mn a quarter to Mar-2028 (~₹665 cr in FY27E, ~₹17.4 of EPS). It roughly offsets IGI's research bill, which stays after the income stops. Q1FY27's 20.0% EBITDA margin was 16.6% without it. We treat the whole upfront as a one-off and forecast no milestones or royalties.

arguments.h: The branded business underneath is genuinely good
arguments.p: India grew 15.5% in Q1FY27 (secondary sales +18.1% vs the market's 12.2%), emerging markets +27.7%, Europe +11.9%; Ryaltris passed US$100mn and grows 40%; Monroe (Nov-2025) and Goa (Sep-2026) were cleared by the USFDA, and North America core sales grew 19.8% on the first respiratory launches.

arguments.h: The record says haircut the promises
arguments.p: Exceptional charges in five straight years (₹261 cr to ₹2,266 cr), two India destocking episodes in two years, negative operating cash flow in FY24 and FY25, margin targets missed (23% by FY27 promised in 2022; 21-22% guided now), and Indore still under a USFDA warning letter. Debt was repaid twice with one-off money (the GLS sale, the AbbVie upfront).

arguments.h: Valuation: the price already pays for the plan
arguments.p: Glenmark's comparable forward P/E has two regimes since 2021: ~16x in its debt-and-warning-letter years and ~32x since the AbbVie deal; the ex-trough median is 20.2x. 22x Sep-28E core EPS gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}, and EV/EBITDA and the DCF are also below the price. The strongest counter-argument is the house median on reported EPS (29.6x), which would give ~₹2,590, a HOLD; the street's post-Q1 median target is ₹2,567.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): the first full quarter of gFlovent 44; core margin against the 21-22% reported guide and the freight/API squeeze.
US approvals in H2FY27 (gFlovent 110mcg, prescription fluticasone nasal spray, an ipratropium inhaler) and the two sole first-to-file launches late in Q3 and in Q4FY27.
ISB 2001: AbbVie's development decisions and any milestone (none received by Aug-2026); ISB 2301 IND by the end of 2026.
Launches in India and emerging markets: Aumolertinib (H2FY27), Trastuzumab Rezetecan filings (from Q2FY27), Ryaltris in Brazil (H2FY27).
USFDA re-inspection of Indore; settlements with the remaining US antitrust groups.

sections.title: Industry: India grows ~10-12% with brands; US generics pay only for complexity; biotech value is binary

blocks.p: **India.** The Indian pharmaceutical market (IPM) grew 10.0% in the twelve months to Jun-2026 and 12.2% in the Apr-Jun 2026 quarter (IQVIA, as quoted by Glenmark). Growth is roughly half volume, a quarter new products and a quarter price; prices of drugs on the price-control list (NLEM) can rise only by the wholesale-price index each April. Distribution changed in FY26: the GST rate cut announced in Aug-2025 made distributors run down stock, which hit companies with a three-tier (super-stockist) system like Glenmark far harder than peers using carrying-and-forwarding agents.

**United States.** US generics are a price-erosion business (low-to-mid single digits a year on the base) where profit comes from products few rivals can make: inhalers (MDIs, DPIs), nasal sprays, complex injectables, and first-to-file or CGT exclusivities worth 180 days or more. Approvals depend on plant inspections: an Official Action Indicated (OAI) rating or a warning letter blocks new approvals from that site.

**Europe and emerging markets.** Europe is a mix of tendered generics and branded products. Glenmark is shifting to brands (respiratory: Ryaltris and MDIs; dermatology: Winlevi, Hilkota), ~30% of its European sales today with a target of ~60% in five years (CMD, Q1FY27 call). Emerging markets (Russia/CIS, Latin America, Middle East & Africa, Asia-Pacific) are branded-generic markets where Glenmark ranks 8th in Russian dermatology (IQVIA) and Ryaltris is the leading allergy nasal spray in most launched markets. They carry currency risk (rouble, Latin American currencies) and are the main outlet for in-licensed oncology drugs (Aumolertinib, Trastuzumab Rezetecan, envafolimab) and, eventually, ISB 2001 outside AbbVie's territories.

**Innovation.** Indian companies rarely monetise new drugs; Glenmark's earlier out-licensing deals (oglemilast, melogliptin, 2004-2008) failed in the clinic. ISB 2001 (Jul-2025, US$700mn upfront), which the company calls a landmark deal, changed that; its value from here depends on AbbVie's development decisions, which Glenmark does not control.

blocks.p: Glenmark's North America business has three parts. The **base generics** portfolio (225 products authorised for sale, 53 applications pending) is mostly oral solids, creams and, increasingly, partnered injectables; it suffers yearly price erosion and has not grown: core sales were ₹3,037 cr in FY22 and ₹3,158 cr (~US$357mn) in FY26. The **respiratory push** started to pay in Q1FY27: the first generic of GSK's Flovent HFA 44mcg inhaler (approved Mar-2026, with a 180-day CGT exclusivity from launch) and an OTC fluticasone nasal spray. **Ryaltris**, Glenmark's own allergy nasal spray, has been sold by its own US team since April 2026 after the Hikma partnership ended. Reported North America revenue also carries ₹166 cr a quarter of ISB 2001 income (US$17.5mn), which we strip out: it is a slice of the upfront AbbVie paid in 2025, not sales.

sections.kicker: Segment: India (29% of FY26 core revenue)
sections.title: India: a strong branded franchise (+15.5% in Q1FY27) with a fragile distribution model

blocks.p: Glenmark is No.13 in the Indian market with a 2.37% share (IQVIA MAT Jun-26) but much stronger in its chosen areas: No.2 in dermatology, No.3 in respiratory, No.4 in cardiac, with 11 brands in the market's top 300. About 5,600 medical representatives sell it, with 300-400 added a year. Secondary (pharmacy-level) sales have outgrown the market for three years (1.5x the IPM in FY26). Reported sales are another matter: Glenmark sells through a legacy three-tier system (super-stockists who own the stock), and twice in two years distributors cut inventory sharply: in Q3FY24 (India sales ₹262 cr, when stock points were consolidated) and in Q2FY26 (₹165 cr, after the GST rate change), costing ~₹1,000 cr of sales and an inventory write-down. Q1FY27 was clean: ₹1,432 cr, +15.5%, secondary +18.1% vs the market's 12.2%.

bullets: **Growth mix (CMD):** volume 6-7%, new products ~3%, price 3-4%; management expects 12-15% a year "on a consistent basis".

**What is driving it:** chronic respiratory (the nebulised triple therapy, ~₹70-80 cr in its first year, "the world's first"), the Telma cardiac franchise, dermatology, and oncology brands in-licensed from BeOne (Tevimbra, Brukinsa: ₹100 cr+ in their first 12 months). Aumolertinib (lung cancer, from Hansoh) and Trastuzumab Rezetecan (HER2 ADC, from Hengrui) follow.
**Consumer care:** Glenmark Consumer Care (Candid powder, La Shield, Scalpe) had primary sales of ₹155.8 cr in Q1FY27 (+28%); moved into a wholly owned subsidiary in FY26.
**Diabetes:** declining until FY26 (remogliflozin and teneligliptin lost to generic rivals); generic semaglutide (Glipiq) at ₹20-25 cr annualised should stabilise it, not drive growth.
**Concentration:** the top brands are still Telma and its extensions (an analyst flagged the risk on the Q1 call); management sees strong brands as a strength.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** India is the best business Glenmark owns. We model ₹5,399 cr in FY27E (+45% on a depressed FY26; management said "over ₹4,800 cr", MOSL ₹5,207 cr) and +13% a year after, taking India to 33.7% of revenue by FY29E. The risk is not demand but the channel: a third destocking episode would hit a quarter's profit hard.

sections.title: Europe and emerging markets: half of core revenue, branded, growing 8-15% a year

blocks.p: **Europe** (₹3,101 cr in FY26, +9%) was Glenmark's fastest-growing region for four years (CMD). It sells generics in Western and Central-Eastern Europe and a growing branded list: Ryaltris (with partner Menarini in some markets), eight other respiratory products, and dermatology brands Winlevi (acne; launched in the UK in Q1FY26 and in the Nordics, CEE and Spain in Q1FY27) and Hilkota. Branded products are ~30% of European sales; the target is ~60% in five years. Growth slowed to 11.9% in Q1FY27; management guides high single digits for FY27 and double digits from FY28 as 2-3 respiratory launches land.

**Emerging markets** (₹2,941 cr, +5%; Russia/CIS, Latin America, Middle East & Africa, Asia-Pacific) grew 27.7% in Q1FY27. Glenmark is No.8 in Russian dermatology (IQVIA), and Ryaltris is the leading allergy nasal spray in most markets where it is sold; it launches in Brazil in H2FY27 and was launched in China (Grand Pharma) and Thailand (Organon) in Q4FY26. EM is also where the in-licensed oncology drugs go first (Aumolertinib from H2FY27; Trastuzumab Rezetecan filings from Q2FY27; envafolimab in FY28), with commercial teams built ahead of launch, which is part of why the FY27 margin guide is 21-22% rather than 23%.

These are steady branded businesses, but many of the growth products are in-licensed or partnered (Winlevi from Cassiopea, oncology from Chinese originators), so Glenmark shares the margin. Currency is the swing factor: the rouble and Latin American currencies have hurt reported growth before.

sections.title: ISB 2001: one US$700mn cheque, a US$70mn-a-year research bill, and milestones we do not count

blocks.p: In July 2025 IGI licensed **ISB 2001** (now ABBV-2001), a trispecific antibody for multiple myeloma built on its BEAT platform, to AbbVie: **US$700mn upfront** (received in September 2025), **up to US$1,225mn** in development, regulatory and commercial milestones, and tiered double-digit royalties on sales. AbbVie has the main markets (North America, Europe, Japan, Greater China); Glenmark will sell it in emerging markets. More than 160 patients have been dosed in the Phase 1 TRIgnite study; no milestone had been received by August 2026 (CMD). IGI's next molecule, ISB 2301, is due to enter the clinic (IND) by the end of 2026, and IGI targets one IND a year.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Glenmark's durable assets are its Indian dermatology, respiratory and cardiac brands and its respiratory development skills (Ryaltris is a genuine global product). Its US generics business has no advantage and a weak compliance record, its cost base earns lower margins than Sun, Cipla or Torrent, and IGI's value depends on trials it no longer controls. sections.title: Ten years of volatility: profit peaked in FY17, hit a ₹1,502 cr loss in FY24, and FY26's ₹1,362 cr rests on a one-off licensing deal

blocks.p: Glenmark's reported revenue grew from ₹6,563 cr in FY15 to ₹16,983 cr in FY26, but the headline hides three breaks. First, the API business (Glenmark Life Sciences, ₹1,271 cr of FY22 sales) was sold to Nirma in March 2024, so FY23 onward is restated without it. Second, FY26 includes ₹3,982 cr of income from licensing ISB 2001 to AbbVie: without it FY26 revenue was ₹13,002 cr. Third, India sales collapsed twice when distributors cut stock (Q3FY24 and Q2FY26). Profit has swung even harder: ₹1,109 cr in FY17 (the generic Zetia exclusivity), ₹297 cr in FY23 (a ₹766 cr Zetia antitrust settlement), a ₹1,502 cr loss in FY24, ₹1,047 cr in FY25 and ₹1,362 cr in FY26, which nets the licensing income against ₹2,266 cr of exceptional charges.

blocks.p: Glenmark's cash record is its weakest point. sections.title: Earnings quality: "one-off" charges in five straight years, licensing income inside revenue, and provisions that can flow back

bullets: **Exceptional items every year.** FY22 ₹261 cr, FY23 ₹766 cr (Zetia settlement), FY24 ₹901 cr, FY25 ₹373 cr, FY26 ₹2,266 cr: us generics price-fixing mdl: direct-purchaser class settlement ₹323 cr; us state attorneys general settlement ₹278 cr; united healthcare (zetia end-payor) settlement ₹98 cr; inventory provision after gst 2.0 and the change in inventory model ₹590 cr; receivables and other current assets ₹496 cr; impairment of property, plant and equipment ₹228 cr; legal costs for the litigation ₹140 cr; new labour codes (employee benefits) ₹114 cr. More antitrust groups (end-payors and one other) are still open. We value on EPS before exceptional items, as the batch rule says, but treat litigation as a recurring cost of being in US generics.

**Licensing income inside revenue.** FY26 revenue includes ₹3,982 cr of ISB 2001 income, booked net of ₹830 cr of one-time charges (impairment and closure of the Swiss plant, R&D inventory, legal provisions) that therefore never appeared as expenses. The deferred part (US$17.5mn a quarter to Mar-2028) keeps lifting reported revenue and margin with no cash.

**Undisclosed one-time costs in operating lines.** The one-time IGI management bonus and the deal costs sat in employee and other expenses in Q2FY26 without a figure; our estimate from the cost lines is ~₹720 cr.

**Provisions that can reverse.** The FY26 charges include ₹590 cr against inventory and ₹496 cr against receivables and other assets; the company says any recovery "will add to profitability". Write-backs would flatter future earnings.
**Forex in other income.** FY26 other income of ₹461 cr included a ₹359 cr exchange gain; interest income was only ₹41 cr. We forecast no forex.

**Quasi-debt behind "zero debt".** A US$96mn (₹879 cr) customer advance received in March 2026, customer security deposits up from ₹132 cr to ₹535 cr, and ₹964 cr of litigation payables, against ₹1,176 cr of net cash.
**Cash conversion.** Operating cash flow was negative in FY24 and FY25; FY26 was positive only because of the upfront and the advance.

**Audit.** Walker Chandiok & Co (Grant Thornton network), unmodified opinion; revenue recognition is a key audit matter. Analysts on the Q4FY26 call asked for consistent disclosure of net debt, capex and R&D, which varies quarter to quarter.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: RED.** Nothing here is illegal or hidden (it is all in the annual report), but a reader of Glenmark's headline numbers has to make five adjustments to see the business: exceptional items every year, licensing income and netted charges inside revenue, undisclosed one-time costs, possible provision write-backs and customer money that props up the cash figure. That is why our model and valuation use core numbers.

sections.title: Balance sheet: "zero gross debt", but ₹1,843 cr of debt-like items; we model net debt of ₹1,219 cr at Mar-26

blocks.p: Glenmark met its promise of zero bank debt at March 2026 and reports net cash of ₹1,176 cr. Look closer and the cushion is thin. It owes ₹594 cr of leases, ₹964 cr of litigation settlements and provisions (US antitrust cases, payable over about two years), and it holds a ₹879 cr advance from a customer for supplies over 3.3 years (US$96mn, received in March 2026), which will be "repaid" in product without new cash. Treating those as debt, the opening net position in our model is −₹1,219 cr. A further ₹1,314 cr of ISB 2001 income received in advance is not debt (it will be booked as revenue with no cash), and customer security deposits rose from ₹132 cr to ₹535 cr. Receivables jumped from ₹3,342 cr to ₹4,963 cr in FY26 after pre-collections stopped; the CFO puts net working capital at ~107 days against a 115-120 day ceiling.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a better Glenmark than in 2023, priced as if the Investor Day plan has already worked

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's No.13 drug maker with leading dermatology, respiratory and cardiac brands growing 12-15% a year; branded Europe and emerging-market businesses (half of core revenue); a US generics arm that finally grew again in Q1FY27 on respiratory launches, with Monroe and Goa cleared; a real global brand in Ryaltris; and IGI, whose ISB 2001 could still pay up to US$1.225bn in milestones. The balance sheet has no bank debt, but ₹964 cr of litigation payables and a ₹879 cr customer advance sit against ₹1,176 cr of net cash.

**What you are paying:** ₹2,335, 31.9x our FY28E core EPS and 28.9x Sep-28E (26.0x on the street's reported basis), against a 20.2x median on comparable EPS since 2021. On the street's method and our numbers the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): a SELL. EV/EBITDA (₹1,811) and the DCF (₹1,321) agree the price is ahead of the fundamentals. exhibit.title: Terms used in this report
head: Term
Meaning
rows: Abbreviated New Drug Application (a generic) / New Drug Application / Investigational New Drug application (permission to start human trials), filed with the USFDA.
Active pharmaceutical ingredient: the drug substance itself (Glenmark Life Sciences, sold in 2024).
IGI's technology for making antibodies that bind several targets at once (bispecific, trispecific, multispecific).
Competitive Generic Therapy: 180 days of exclusivity for the first approved generic of a drug with little competition (Glenmark's gFlovent 44mcg).
Our basis: excluding all ISB 2001 licensing income (the upfront booked in Q2FY26 and the deferred slices to Mar-2028), and before exceptional items.
Part of the AbbVie upfront (US$175mn) received in cash in 2025 but booked as revenue at US$17.5mn a quarter until Mar-2028.
Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Screener and company basis; excludes other income and exceptional items).
Establishment Inspection Report closing a USFDA inspection / Voluntary Action Indicated (minor findings) / Official Action Indicated (serious) / formal letter that blocks new approvals from a site.
Enterprise value (market value plus debt minus cash) divided by EBITDA.
Large charges or gains shown separately in the accounts (Glenmark: litigation settlements, inventory and receivable provisions, impairments, labour codes).
The first generic applicant challenging a patent, eligible for 180 days of exclusivity ("sole" if no one shares it).
Share price divided by the next full fiscal year's EPS.
Ichnos Glenmark Innovation: Glenmark's US/Swiss biotech subsidiary (ISB 2001, ISB 2301 and others).
Indian pharmaceutical market / the data provider that tracks pharmacy sales / sales from distributors to pharmacies (what patients buy), as opposed to the company's primary sales to distributors.
Metered-dose inhaler (Flovent, Atrovent generics) / spray into the nose (Ryaltris) / device turning liquid medicine into a mist (Glenmark's triple therapy in India).
Payment due when a licensed drug reaches a stage (trial start, approval, sales level) / a percentage of the drug's sales.
Glenmark's former practice of collecting cash from distributors before the due date at a discount (up to ~20% cost, per the CFO); stopped in FY26, which raised receivables.
The median of the nine-peer pharma set's P/E at 30-Sep-2026 vs their five-year medians (+8.2%), applied to Glenmark's own historical multiple.
Half of FY28E EPS plus half of FY29E EPS: the twelve-month-forward EPS the market will look at in September 2027, when the target falls due.

A forward year whose EPS was a loss or below half the best of the previous three years (FY24 and FY26 on our core basis; FY23 and FY24 on reported EPS); left out of the historical median because the P/E balloons when profit collapses.

businessLines._why: FY26 revenue by region (AR FY26 segment table): India Rs3,723.7 cr, North America Rs7,139.0 cr = core Rs3,157.5 cr + ISB 2001 income Rs3,981.5 cr (Rs3,670.0 cr booked net in Q2FY26 = US$525mn Rs4,500 cr less Rs830 cr of one-time charges netted in revenue, plus Rs311.5 cr of deferred income in H2, note 19), Europe Rs3,100.7 cr, emerging markets Rs2,940.5 cr, other revenue Rs78.6 cr. Total Rs16,982.5 cr = Screener revenue. North America core in US dollars x an assumed rupee rate (FY26 Rs88.33/$; Q1FY27 Rs94.53).

assumptions._marginWhy: Core EBITDA margin (excluding ISB 2001 income, after IGI's R&D): FY26 core EBITDA Rs591 cr (4.5% of core revenue Rs13,001 cr) was crushed by the India destocking and the one-time IGI bonus and deal costs; H2FY26 core 18.0% (Q3 19.0%, Q4 16.8%); Q1FY27 core 16.6% (reported 20.0% = Rs804.8 cr incl. Rs165.5 cr deferred income). Guidance: 21-22% reported for FY27 (incl. the ~Rs665 cr deferred income, worth ~3.5pp), i.e. ~17.5-18.5% core. FY27E 17.8% core = 21.0% on the reported basis (bottom of guidance: Q1 was 20.0%, freight and API costs up, oncology launch spending). FY28E 19.0% core (~21.9% reported: management's ~1pp improvement from operating leverage, US respiratory and injectables, branded mix). FY29E 19.8%: the deferred income stops in Mar-2028, so reported and core converge; without milestones, the reported margin would fall from ~21.9% to ~19.8% that year. IGI's ~US$70mn a year (about half of group R&D of 7-8% of sales) stays in all three years. Street FY27E: MOSL 20.9%, Choice 21.0% (both reported, incl. deferred income). Each 1pp of FY28E margin is ~Rs183 cr of EBITDA (~6% of EPS).
assumptions._capexWhy: CFO (Q4FY26 call): FY26 was a one-off with 'close to Rs800 cr plus' of intangibles (in-licensing upfronts and milestones for oncology/dermatology, US injectable partnerships) on top of Rs1,358 cr of fixed-asset purchases (Screener); FY27 'around Rs900 cr sort of capex number total'. FY28-29E Rs950 / 1,000 cr (~5% of sales), including further in-licensing milestones (Aumolertinib, Trastuzumab Rezetecan, envafolimab). Acquisitions not modelled.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation, amortisation and impairment Rs573.5 cr; Q1FY27 Rs173 cr (Rs692 cr annualised) after FY26's intangibles and the Rs594 cr of new leases. 5.6% of average gross block (Screener Rs12,072 cr at Mar-26 plus capex) gives Rs701 / 753 / 808 cr for FY27-29E, matching the Q1 run-rate in FY27E.

otherTreasury._why: Debt-like items taken out of the opening net cash (AR FY26 notes 14-18): litigation liabilities and provisions Rs963.6 cr (Rs403.9 cr current and Rs281.6 cr non-current financial liabilities, Rs101.5 cr and Rs176.6 cr provisions; payable over ~2 years per management) and the Rs879.2 cr customer advance (US$96mn received Mar-2026 under a 3.3-year supply contract, to be repaid in product). Model opening net cash = Screener cash Rs1,176 cr + investments Rs42 cr - leases Rs594 cr - Rs1,843 cr = -Rs1,219 cr, against the company's net cash of Rs1,176 cr (which excludes leases and these items). The Rs1,314 cr of ISB 2001 income received in advance is non-cash and is NOT treated as debt; it stays in operating liabilities.

assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied by the engine to the model's net cash when positive (it is negative at Mar-26 after the debt-like items, so it adds nothing in FY27E and a little from FY28E). 5%: FY26 interest income Rs41.3 cr on ~Rs1,200-2,700 cr of average cash; Indian treasury rates ~5-6%.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from AR FY26 note 20 and Q1FY27: (a) interest on operating cash (~Rs800-900 cr held, CFO) Rs40 cr (FY26 Rs41.3 cr); (b) working-capital 'interest-rate arbitrage' income Rs140 / 145 / 150 cr, which the CFO says now sits in other income while the matching cost sits in finance cost (Q1FY27 other income Rs66 cr = ~Rs40 cr arbitrage + ~Rs11 cr interest + ~Rs15 cr misc); (c) miscellaneous income Rs60 / 65 / 70 cr (FY26 Rs60.1 cr). Forex gains (Rs359.2 cr in FY26) and the ISB 2001 income are not forecast. FY27E Rs240 cr vs Rs460.6 cr in FY26 (Rs101 cr ex forex) and Rs264 cr Q1-annualised.
assumptions._interestLabel: Finance cost (leases, bank charges, working-capital arbitrage)
assumptions._interestWhy: No borrowings since Mar-26, but Q1FY27 finance cost was Rs54 cr (Rs216 cr annualised): interest on Rs594 cr of leases (~Rs50 cr a year at ~9%), bank commitment charges and the cost side of the working-capital arbitrage whose income is in other income (CFO). FY26 Rs208.7 cr (bank loans Rs120.8 cr, repaid). Rs215 / 205 / 195 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: Q1FY27 ETR 24.9% (tax Rs160 cr on PBT Rs643 cr); FY25 25.2%; IGI's Swiss/US losses get little tax relief, so the group rate stays above India's 25.2%. MOSL 27.5%. 26% flat.
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend Rs5.0 a share (~10% of reported EPS, ~Rs141 cr cash); FY25 Rs2.5. 8% of core EPS (~Rs5 a share).

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash only after the AbbVie upfront; a history of USFDA warning letters (three sites since 2022), US antitrust settlements in three of the last four years, two India destocking episodes and a loss year (FY24). Ke 12.5%, above Lupin (11.9%) and Cipla (11.3%).
dcf._tgWhy: 5.5%: India 10-12% nominal, emerging markets and Europe high single digit, US generics flat to low single digit in dollars.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 21% core: the branded mix (India, EM, European respiratory and dermatology, oncology in-licensing) lifts margins slowly, but IGI's burn continues unless milestones arrive; the company's own 23% (2022 target) was not met.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex 5% of revenue (FY27E 5.5% incl. in-licensing); depreciation 4% of revenue (FY27E 4.3%).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: The Investor Day plan works: 13-15% growth, US respiratory approvals and the two first-to-files land on time, Monroe ramps, Aumolertinib and Trastuzumab Rezetecan scale in India and EM, Ryaltris heads for US$250-300mn, margins reach ~23%.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: US launches slip (Indore stays under the warning letter, respiratory approvals delayed), another India channel disruption, more US litigation charges and freight/API costs keep core margin near 16-17%.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Glenmark: both brokers that disclose a method use P/E (Motilal Oswal 25x 12-month-forward EPS plus a Rs290 NPV for ISB 2001; Deven Choksey 25x Sep-27E EPS in its Jan-2026 note). 22x = Glenmark's 20.2x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 on EPS before exceptional items and before the ISB 2001 licensing income (batch practice A18; the upfront treated as a one-off), leaving out the trough years FY24 (a loss) and FY26 (core EPS Rs7.2, below half of FY25's Rs47.0), times the pharma sector factor of 1.082 (median of the nine-peer set's trailing P/E at the 30-Sep close vs their five-year medians: +8.2%, PLAYBOOK §7c A20; Glenmark is outside the set) = 21.9x, rounded to the nearest half-turn. No growth or returns adjustment and no separate value for IGI/ISB 2001 (only one of the two brokers that disclose a method adds it; shown as a sensitivity). Bull 34.5x and bear 17.5x: the 75th (31.7x) and 25th (16.2x) percentiles of the same series times the same factor.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Own one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021 (EV = price x 28.22 cr shares + Screener net debt at the latest March; EBITDA = next full year, FY26 on a core basis excluding the ISB 2001 income, ours for FY27-28E): median 11.9x leaving out the FY26 trough (core EBITDA Rs591 cr), times the EV/EBITDA analogue of the sector factor for the same nine peers (+7.46%) = 12.8x, rounded to 13x; bull/bear from the 75th/25th percentiles (17.9x / 11.0x). The engine adds the model net cash at Sep-28 (after the debt-like items), a year beyond the target date.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at a 12.5% cost of equity, terminal growth 5.5%, core margin fading to 21%, plus the model's net cash (after debt-like items).
